paper.title_en: Numerical simulation of noise impact on DWDM-based MP-QKD in multi-user scenarios
paper.abstract_en: Quantum key distribution (QKD) guarantees the theoretical security of communication based on the principles of quantum mechanics and serves as a core component of quantum communication networks. To address the challenge of enabling multi-user concurrent communication and improving transmission efficiency, the integration of dense wavelength division multiplexing (DWDM) technology with QKD protocols has emerged as an important research direction. This paper focuses on the performance of the MP-QKD protocol based on DWDM in multi-user scenarios, analyzing the impact of key parameters such as the number of channels, different noise type, channel isolation, classical channel power, and detector configuration on the system noise rate and secret key rate through numerical simulations. The results demonstrate that DWDM technology can enhance the total secret key capacity through multi-channel parallel transmission, while optimizing channel isolation, classical channel power, channel count, and detector configuration can effectively suppress noise interference and improve system performance. These findings provide useful guidance for the practical deployment of multi-user quantum communication networks with low noise and high performance.
